turns.text: ok need help w inventory models. ops management midterm is oct 23 and i lowkey never got EOQ. can you explain th formula pls

Sure. EOQ finds the order size that minimizes total yearly ordering cost plus holding cost.

EOQ = √(2DS / H)

- D = annual demand (units/year)
- S = cost per order (fixed cost each time you place one)
- H = holding cost per unit per year

Bigger orders mean fewer orders (lower ordering cost) but more stock sitting around (higher holding cost). EOQ is the point where those two costs are equal.

Quick example: D = 1,200 units, S = $50, H = $6. EOQ = √(2·1200·50 / 6) = √20,000 ≈ 141 units, so about 8.5 orders a year.

Good question, exams love this. EOQ assumes:

1. Demand is constant and known
2. Lead time is constant and known
3. Order cost and holding cost don't change with order size (no quantity discounts)
4. The whole order arrives at once
5. No stockouts allowed

If demand or lead time varies, you add safety stock on top of EOQ. That's the next piece.

Glad that call went well. TLDR:

Safety stock = z × σ_LT

- z = z-score for your target service level (90% ≈ 1.28, 95% ≈ 1.65, 99% ≈ 2.33)
- σ_LT = standard deviation of demand during lead time

If demand varies per day with std dev σ_d and lead time is L days: σ_LT = σ_d × √L

Reorder point = (average daily demand × L) + safety stock

Example: σ_d = 20 units/day, L = 9 days, 95% service. σ_LT = 20 × 3 = 60. Safety stock = 1.65 × 60 ≈ 99 units.
